title: Standard MHA, three schedules
formula: out = softmax(Q @ K^T * scale) @ V per batch and head, BSND, D=128, FP16 or BF16
study_for: Three schedules behind one kernel signature. `head_resident` keeps one head's K/V on chip and runs QK for the current item against a delayed PV for the previous one; `head_preload` widens the K/V pipeline to three slots and a 256-key tile for long causal prefill; `packed_decode` packs many one-query items into a single physical M128 tile. A case selects one by name and changes nothing else, so the three are directly comparable.

`weighted_partition` in kernel.py is host-only work: it partitions batch*head*query-group items across 28 cores by their causal key weight, elaborating the cut table as literals. It is neither a GM allocation nor a kernel argument, and it is a worked example of deciding a grid on the host instead of branching on the device.

How a demo stays runnable without a card: every full-shape case has a `model` counterpart shrunk around one named behaviour — a one-query tail, a head that must not be shared, an equal-but-not-aliased K/V pair, a zero input against a poisoned output. main.py runs the model cases under sim and skips the full ones with a reason.

The zero/nonzero pair. `model_resident_zero` feeds zeros into a NaN-poisoned output: the result is legitimately all zeros, so it only proves anything because `model_resident_nonzero` runs the identical signature with real values. A zero case alone cannot tell a correct kernel from one that writes nothing.
do_not_copy_when: You need GQA or MQA. Every head here owns independent K and V; a shared-KV layout changes the partition, the on-chip residency and the P publication together.
Your head dimension is not 128. D=128 is what makes one head's K/V tile fit the on-chip budget these three schedules were tiled against.
You want the smallest possible attention example. This is a complete kernel with tails, causal boundaries and three schedules — read a5_v8_cube_stage or a5_v8_p_stage for a single stage in isolation.
